intended_object: A half-plane in ℝ² bounded by the line ⟪p, n(t)⟫ = h, where n(t) = (cos t, sin t) is the unit normal at angle t. It is closed or open (`strict`) and lies on the upper side ⟪p,n⟫ ≥ h or the lower side ⟪p,n⟫ ≤ h (`upper`). Inferred from the docstring, the name and nearby uses (normalLine, supportingLineHalfPlane).
explanation: The body gives exactly the four half-planes {h < ⟪p,n(t)⟫}, {h ≤ ⟪p,n(t)⟫}, {⟪p,n(t)⟫ < h} and {⟪p,n(t)⟫ ≤ h}, where n(t) = (cos t, sin t) is a unit vector. This matches the docstring: `upper` selects the greater side and `strict` the open version. The surrounding lemmas (closedness, convexity, use as the supporting half-plane) agree with this reading. Parametrising the normal by a `Real.Angle` only makes sense in the plane, and the moving sofa problem is planar, so working on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) is what the content needs; it is not an artificial restriction. Mathlib has no named half-space definition, only lemmas such as convex_halfSpace_le about sets {x | f x ≤ r}.
